Use `snl library move-entry` to move one existing Library occurrence without changing Entry identity.

### Command path
`library/move-entry` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The shell adapter is `snl library move-entry`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"library/move-entry","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"id":"<library-slug>","entryId":"<exact-entry-id>","occurrenceId":null,"parentOccurrenceId":null,"beforeOccurrenceId":null,"expectedRevision":"<opaque>"}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Ambiguous Entry identity is never accepted where an occurrence identity is required.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"library/move-entry","data":...,"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains the changed occurrence and canonical Library readback with new revision.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"library/move-entry","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":...,"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Mutating. Bind Library revision under the shared lock, validate node/edge identities and projected acyclic topology, then durably publish all graph files together or roll back. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. After success, canonical readback and whole-workspace validation must observe the published state.
